mapping_basis: Neither type_list.csv nor synonyms.csv lists 'foxglove'; driver_lines.csv lists foxglove line SS40909 (VT019012-AD;VT022244-DBD, hemidrivers reversed vs. this genotype) as UNMAPPED and says the source does not state whether foxglove is a DN; this paper does not say either.
n_flies_note: 9 experiments, 6 targeted flies each (6-8 flies introduced per experiment)
notes: Stopping is inferred only from centroid tracking (flies staying in goal regions under laser) used as a tool, not a controlled activation test; no no-retinal or empty-split control reported. Whether foxglove is a descending neuron is not established by this source or the kit; adjudication should confirm DN status before use. The paper does not describe the line's expression pattern.
penetrance: not quantified per fly; all 6 flies held formation simultaneously, 9 experiments (Fig. 8H-J)
quote: This was achieved by expressing the red-shifted channelrhodopsin, CsChrimson, in neurons that cause flies to stop walking [“foxglove halting neurons” (56)]
sensory_condition: freely walking in 43 cm arena, IR backlight, projected blue/black pinwheel used for guidance before stimulation
source_locator: Results, 'Multifly Control—Formation Control with Flies'; Fig. 8F-J; SI Appendix Table S1 (row 8F-J)
stimulation: 640 nm red laser steered by galvo mirrors, 4-4.5 mW over ~5 mm beam (51 µW/mm2), mirrors dwell ~10 ms per fly at ~100 Hz; switched on once the fly reached its goal area
title: The fruit fly, Drosophila melanogaster, as a microrobotics platform.
